title: An agent can watch its own video and tell whether it is smooth, on the beat and readable
goal: Today an agent can only look at still frames, so it cannot tell if its reel stutters, jitters, misses the beat or flashes text too fast to read. Give it a way to watch: measured reports on a span of the video that say where motion is rough, where cuts miss the music and where words are on screen too briefly.
notes:
User, 2026-11-24: "I also want to have the agent make high quality 'sizzle reels'... What prevents us from having enough control to make high videlity sizzle reals that really slap. I'm talking apple smoothness coupled with high energy music that builds as we demonstrate features of aplications. And the features are smooth - we capture the most credible moments of an app, making the user really pumped to use them. With creshendos that build up and reveal something massive. We need video features that can do that. Help refine the flows and ensure that agents have the tools to do this".

What agents can reach today (checked 2026-11-24, plugin/skills/photonz/SKILL.md and the MCP tool list): new_video, add_clip, move_clip, trim, cut, add_title, list_titles, set_transition, apply_zooms, recommended_zooms (from recorded clicks), set_keys / change_keys with named curves, video_frame, contact_sheet, export, list_history. NOT reachable by an agent: music or any sound placement and levels, beats of any kind (nothing in Sources analyses tempo or beats), speed changes (the app has setSpeed and speed stops as commands, no agent tool), recording the screen or driving the app being shown, and any way to judge motion rather than stills. Exists in the app but not checked for agent reach: motion smear (MotionSmearFilter), depth transitions, keyframe curves, title entrances.
acceptance: An agent tool renders a span of the timeline exactly as export would and reports: frames with a hitch (motion that steps instead of flowing), text or edges that jitter apart from their layer (the jitter measure from text-that-zooms-or-scales-in-a-video-moves-as-on), blank or flashing frames, cuts and title hits measured against the nearest beat or bar (needs the beats task; until then against a supplied beat list), and every line of text with its time on screen against the time needed to read it.
It also gives the pictures that matter: frames on each cut, at each section change, and a strip of the busiest motion, so the agent's eyes go where the problems are.
Each measure is checked against a hand-made case that has the fault and one that does not, in unit tests first; numbers in the audit.

The skill tells agents to run it after every meaningful change to a reel and fix what it reports before exporting. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.
